title: Applied Materials, Intel target AI chip bottlenecks with interconnect scaling and Foveros 3D
key_facts: Applied Materials announced on 6 Oct that Intel has joined the EPIC Center as a founding partner.
They will jointly develop process technologies and equipment across front-end, back-end-of-line and packaging stages.
Work includes new logic materials and device architectures, advanced interconnect, and Foveros-based 3D stacking.
Applied provides Intel a dedicated secure space inside the EPIC Center; Intel connects its Hillsboro, Oregon, R&D campus.
The centre has more than 10 participating companies including Samsung, SK hynix, Micron, TSMC and Broadcom.
Opening ceremony scheduled for 12 Oct (THE ELEC).
quote_evidence: Applied Materials stated on October 6 that Intel has joined the Applied EPIC Center as a founding partner.
Applied Materials will provide Intel with a dedicated secure space inside the EPIC Center.
Its opening ceremony is scheduled for October 12.
why_it_matters_hint: Shortens the lab-to-fab path for US advanced chips; goals only.
notes: Digitimes page (7 Oct) shows only a lead; facts read at THE ELEC and Unite.AI, both rewriting Applied Materials' 6 Oct announcement (Unite.AI quotes both CEOs). Investment is given as 7 trillion won by THE ELEC and $5 billion in Besi/DQ text; not used in summary.
